note: RI-DLG02: rumours MUST differ per town. RI-CHR02 §4c: '>= 2 race-specific rumours per settlement = 16'. Round 1 shipped 0 race-gated. A race-gated rumour is the same town gossiping differently at you: the square does not say the same sentence to a Saxhleel and to a Dunmer, and what it declines to say is the content.
w1_19_note: W1-19 round 2 added the main-quest rumours and the `adds_topics` field. Round 1 measurement: **0 rumour lines anywhere in game/data/dialogue/** named a main-quest noun**, and this file had no code consumer at all — it was loaded into `data.rumours` at engine.js and read by nothing after that. Under seam S8 there are no markers, so gossip is not decoration: it is the only thing that can tell a player who has just stepped off a barge what words to say to the Undersexton at Soulrest. A rumour carrying `adds_topics` puts those words into `sim.quest.topicsKnown` (see `game/src/sim/quest/topic-supply.js RumourBook`, read by `Conversation` via `Engine._installTopicSupply`), which is the only route into `Q-MAIN-01` that owes nothing to a prior quest. Existing rows are untouched; every addition is additive and the file is still declared incomplete for W1-11's own coverage.

thorn: The king pays in fish because he has nothing else, and he pays.
Something took the Ghen boy's boat and left the boy.

thorn.x: Soulrest hasn't read the Drowned Tally on time, and the king's own dead are in it. He's said nothing about that in the hall. And he's said a great deal about it in the yard.
The tree behind the hall has been saying the same four words since Second Seed, and Sesh-Anaat has stopped writing them down. Have you been up to the hall?
The Saltgirl is nine metres down on the bar mouth with a man still in her, and his widow is asking after the log rather than the man.
The old causeway to Salt Hills is still there under the water. You can feel the stones with a pole. No one has walked it since the tide came up. Would you?
There's a guar standing in the herbwife's yard that isn't hers, won't move, and has been there since the rain stopped. Whose do you suppose it is?
The house at the end of the walk has had swamp-rot in the timbers two seasons and the family are still in it, and everyone has agreed not to say so.
The widow on the stilts is carrying something broken in a cloth and will not put it down, and the family will not speak to her until it is whole.
A hunter walked back out of the deep marsh standing up and has not moved since. He is warm and he is looking at us.

It isn't the weather shutting the tracks north. It's the Naga-Kur and they're standing inside the gate now, which the warders have decided not to notice. So the Office writes it up as a seasonal hazard for the fourth year running.
The charter says Thorn is a village and a village pays no gate fee, and Gideon has stopped answering letters about the charter, and the fee is being collected.
The tree has been quiet since the coast business and the keepers are up at it in the dark, which they do not do. And they are not singing.
A man walked out of the deep marsh standing up and has not moved since, and Ossa will not say he is alive and will not say the other thing.
The tide-turn walk was made three days early this month and the whole village went, and no one has explained the hurry.
The tree took water again. It is the whole of what anyone here will tell you, and they tell it as though it settles the matter. Does it?
The keepers let an outlander stand at the tree and the village has not decided yet whether to be angry about it.

stormhold: The Legion hasn't been paid since Sun's Height, and the customs house knows it.
There's a milestone on the pass road that gives a distance to a place you can't find.

stormhold.x: There is a mortuary town down the coast that has missed a reading of the Drowned Tally for the first time in four hundred years, and the prefect has been sent three letters about it and answered none.
Eleven boxes came off an imperial bond at Archon and got to Soulrest weighing what an empty box weighs. The customs house calls that a customs matter and would rather it wasn't one.
Sedd wants six crates of lamp oil out of the quarter behind the north wall and will not send a soldier in for them. He says it is stores now and perfectly safe, and he says it twice.
Someone has been walking the archive after the lamps go out, and that floor is boards over empty air — it can't be walked quietly. The scribe there wants a name.
Hulen's assistant fills four pages a day and can't tell you what's on any of them. He can still write. He can't read. Did you ever know him before?
The potter out at the wastes kiln dropped a whole firing down the flue, and no one has ever written down when that flue is hot.
The salt market weighed short three days running and the weigh house says the scale is fine. The scale has been fine for thirty years. Do you see the difficulty?
Okan-Shei has not undercut a rival in thirty years and this month he undercut the whole west end, and the market is trying to work out what he knows.
There was a light behind the north wall on the eleventh and the watch that saw it has been moved to the harbour gate. Moved, mind. Not disciplined. What do you make of that?
Something is living in the drains that the engineers cut and the garrison will not go down and the town has stopped asking them to.
The night watch has been doubled and the reason given is thieves. There have been no thieves. But there has been a great deal of walking about at night by men in Legion boots.
A family on Wall Street is still paying rent on a house behind the wall and the Office still takes it. Nine years now. Not one clerk will say the house exists.
The quartermaster has been selling boots to the town and buying worse ones for the cohort, and the tribune knows. So who do you suppose is wearing the good pair?
The border road has had two carts go missing off it this season and the third one came back with everything on it and no driver.
There are names on the muster board that have drawn pay since before the fever year, and the man who noticed has been posted to a fort with no roof. Would you notice anything, in his place?
The old ones here still measure a bad year against the six that came after the fever, and they will tell you this one is not close, and they will tell you it is the same shape.
There is a back route out of the inn on the eleventh of the month, for people who would rather not meet the Tribune coming in, and it is busier than the front.
Belena Sarn has not signed a warrant in six weeks and the pile is on her desk where the whole office can see it. Courage or a message, take your pick.
They are cutting new cisterns into the salt rock and the water that comes up is not fit and they are cutting anyway.
The gate fee went up by a third and the notice went up after the fee did. Two carters have refused to pay and have not been stopped, and the gate has noticed.
A clerk went into the old quarter with a lamp and a book last winter to make a survey of it and came out and asked to be transferred.
The cohort has been counting its own wells since the coast business and it has found it has fewer than the roll says. You only find that out by walking to them.
There is an order posted about the salt trade that no one will read out loud and the market has decided it means the Empire is short of money.
Two men came up from the marsh asking after the old quarter and had papers for it, and the gate let them through, and the gate has been quiet about whose papers.
The tribune has stopped drinking at the inn. He has been at the weigh house instead, in the evenings, with the books out.
The garrison has been told to expect a movement of water in the drains and has not been told by whom, and the men are treating that as an order about a flood.
Half the border traffic stopped this month and the road is not closed. It has simply gone quiet, the way a road does when the people who used it have found a reason not to.
Whatever happened under the wastes, the salt rock felt it, and there are new cracks in the cistern floor that the engineers are recording as settlement.
The Office has begun a survey of every well in the province and it is being done properly. After all this, that is either shame or a bill being prepared.
A stranger got into the old quarter and came out and did not go to the Office about it. The garrison would very much like to know what was seen.
The dead pay got said out loud in front of a clerk who wrote it down, and the muster board has been repainted since. Coincidence, is it?
The paymaster is finished and there is a stranger in this town who is said to have done it with arithmetic. The men cannot decide whether that is worse.
The weigh house books went to Gideon in a locked case and came back in a sack, and the clerk who signed for them has asked to be moved.

soulrest.x: The Undersexton's been asking after a hand off the customs bench who can count and can't be leaned on. Her name's Rell, and she takes the reading room after noon.
Eleven boxes came up from the quay and went into the low chapel and a sexton has been on that door ever since.
The Ladder well's gone cold, and the keeper hasn't left the rim. The carters will tell you so on the coast road. They won't tell you so in here!
The undertaker behind the customs post has been counting her own dead against the Court's book and getting a different answer two years running. She is asking after a hand that is not of the Court.

The Court has burial figures going back four hundred years and they say the estate-hatched come up heavy and come up young. Ask a sexton about the copper cup at Gideon. Then watch how fast he finds something to carry.
The yard behind the customs post has burned more this year than the Court's book admits, and the woman who burns them keeps her own count and will show it to anyone who asks.
The bone-setter here has taken to refusing warmbloods and giving a different reason each time. Two of the reasons contradicted each other in the same afternoon. Are you well?
The listening is kept at the turn of the tide and the town arranges its evenings round it, and the customs post has begun writing down who attends.
There have been drums out over the flats and not every night, and the ones who have been counting the nights have stopped telling people the pattern.
The silted bay took a keel this month that drew less water than the last one that got through, and the pilots are arguing about whether the bay is moving.
The wells here went first and no one up the coast believed it, and now that they do believe it they have begun explaining it to us.
The Tally went out late this year and the Court sent to ask why, and the clerk who wrote the reply has been drinking since.
The Court has taken a room at the customs post and paid for a season, and the post has never let a room before.
The count came right this year for the first time in three, and the woman at the yard has not said a word about it. So the town knows it is true.
The salt pans out on the point are worked by three families and one of them has not been seen this season, and the other two are working all three pans and saying nothing about it.
A stranger counted the dead again, properly, and the two books came out the same, and the Court has not thanked anyone for it.

gideon.x: Soulrest is late with the Drowned Tally, and the Wet Ledger's already worked out what that's worth. Ask the porter on the quay. He said it once and he won't say it twice.
You can't walk into the Archon bond store as yourself. Four houses in this town will lend you a name, and every one of them wants a different thing back.
The market cross is where the coast road ends and the crypt road starts, and only one of those two is on a chart.
Every porter under the crane has been paid eleven gold a week short since Rain's Hand and the shortfall has no name on it. Eeja can give you the number to the coin. Ask her!
The shrine-house on the low market has no door on the street side, a guard on the other, and one window, and it is barred.
Two clerks, one lamp, and a strongbox that is only open between the eighth and ninth bell. Ashul talks about it more than a man should.
There is a woman in this town who is the only person who saw it, and the Assize will not say why she will not say so.
They found a courier dead in an alley with his fee still on him. So whatever he was killed for, he hadn't delivered it yet. Who pays a fee and takes nothing?
The well on the low market has been sealed since Frostfall. Her husband went down after a bucket and she wants what he was carrying, not the well opened.
The old kiln on the low market has not gone cold in years and the yard men will not go near it. Mek walled a firing into it the week his brother died and now he wants it out.
There is a loft with a season's accounts in it and no stair, and the stair was taken out for exactly that reason.
A guar calf is fouled in a net line in deep water and the cow will not let a boat near it. The warden has been standing on the bank about it for two days.
The water under the grange tree runs clear now. It ran black when my mother drew it. The court will not say what that means and two of the Archein have stopped drinking it.
The underwriters' gate refused four manifests in a week and the man with the stamp has been seen drinking at the factor house. He does not drink there.
There is a scribe in this town who was struck off the roll and comes in every morning and does the work. And the notary has stopped pretending not to see her.
The vestry well was sealed for a fortnight and reopened with no notice, and Brother Teleno has been asked about it four times and has answered differently each time. Would you ask a fifth?
The field grid was re-surveyed in the spring and eleven holdings came out smaller and none came out larger, and the surveyor has left the province.
The woman who saw it still walks the same road home past the same door every evening, and the town has decided that means she is lying.
The Assize has cleared a week in its calendar and has not said what for, and three notaries have cancelled travel.
The Office has begun answering letters it has sat on for years and the answers are all the same length. The clerks find that more sinister than the silence.
The vestry well came up brown for a day after the coast business and Brother Teleno had it drawn off and refilled before the morning, and told the vestry it was silt.
The Assize has begun asking the yards about their water rather than their leases. When did that building last ask about water?
A porter on the quay said something once about the Tally being late and has not been on the quay since, and his crew say he took a berth south.
Four houses in this town will lend you a name and this month three of them stopped, and the fourth has put its price past what a working man has.
The court factor has been going through the lease roll year by year and writing in the margins, and margins are not where that office writes.
They have taken the struck-off notary's name off the roll properly at last, and put it back on, and the office will not say which came first.
The woman who saw it has said what she saw, to a stranger who was not of the court, and the town has gone very quiet about her since.
The lease vote got counted out loud in front of the room. That has not happened here in living memory and two of the chairs have not been back.

archon.x: The Court's reading is late, and the Salt Factor hasn't stopped smiling about it since Second Seed. One of them down there is going to come and ask him for water.
The crane crew know what the sealed crates sound like when they land and will tell you for the price of a drink, provided nothing is written down.
The vats flooded twice this season and the lung wage has not moved, and the men who mix have stopped pretending the two are unconnected. How long would you mix, at that wage?
The purple law is enforced on the dye yards and on no one else, and the yard office will tell you that is because no other house dyes.
The militia here is nine men and a list, and the list has three names on it that belong to the dead, and the pay still goes out.
The tide lichen has come in thick on the north bank and the healers are calling it a good sign, and the old ones are not.
The chapel bell rang on its own again and the priest went on with what he was saying. That frightened the congregation rather more than the bell had!
The water call was held early this year and half the town was not told, and the half that was told will not say who told them.
The yard office has taken on a clerk from Gideon who asks about the well rather than the vats, and asks it of the wrong people, politely.
The vats have been run dry twice on purpose this month and the reason given is cleaning. They have never been cleaned.
The dye yards are hiring again and the wage is worse and the queue is longer, and the two facts are being reported as one piece of good news.
The Dres factor has gone from this town and the House has not replaced him, and the market cannot decide whether to be pleased.
The office annexe here has one clerk and four registers and three of the registers are for a trade this town stopped doing forty years ago.
An-Deesei has been buying tide lichen at a price that makes no sense and drying it somewhere the yards have not found.
The crossing fee was set by a man who has been dead eleven years and the ferry still collects it in his name. And the name is still on the board.
There is a healer here who will not treat vat cough any more and will not say why, and she is the only one in the town who was any good at it.
The water call was held twice this year. Twice. The second one was not announced and the people who went will not say who called it.
The vats have been taking water from the far bank since the spring and paying a toll for it that the yard office has not entered anywhere.
The purple law was enforced on a house that does no dyeing at all last month, and the yard office is calling that a clerical matter.
The lung wage went up the week after and no house has claimed credit for it. In this town that means it was not a kindness.
The water call is open to anyone who asks now, and there is a stranger who is said to have argued it open, and the vats are watching to see what it costs.

blackrose.x: The yards send their dead down to Soulrest with the rest, and the Drowned Tally hasn't been read this year. So no word's come back about where they are.
Neeja-Xul lost a blade out of the third yard in Rain's Hand and she hasn't reported it. She reports everything.

The Prefect wants his lease register reconciled before the Elder Council comes, and he will not give it to a clerk. Ask anyone at the fortress what four hundred and eleven means and watch their hands.
Veth has had the older brother in her common room since Sun's Height and the younger one pays for him every week without ever coming in.
The innkeeper has stopped sending anyone down to her own cellar after dark, and has started asking whether a door can be held shut for a whole night. Can it?

There's a Paatru on the roll and he keeps telling the clerks he was taken in the dry season. They keep writing that he came voluntarily to a place of trade. Both of them are saying a true thing and only one of them is on the paper.
They planted roses on the old execution ground and the prison has never once explained it. Every family in this town has a view on what it means. What is yours?
The long sentences are getting longer and the warden signs them and the Assize does not read them, and the warden has begun signing them in front of witnesses.
The one customer took the whole of the timber cut again this season at a price no other yard was offered, and the yards are calling that a contract.
The supply road has been running at night, which it does not, and the prison has taken deliveries it did not order. Both of those at once, mind.
There is a grave on the point with no name cut on it and every person in this town knows the name, and it has stayed uncut for nine years.
The Company has been buying leases at Blackrose it cannot work and paying over the value, and the yards have begun refusing to sell.
The prison took in a body this month that came from the interior and was not a prisoner, and the day book has it as a transfer.
The warden has asked for the long sentences to be reviewed. All of them. He has asked before and this is the first time Gideon has answered!
The warden's petition has gone up three times and come back unopened three times, and he has started reading it out to the yard instead.
The timber yards took on twenty hands and let eighteen go inside a month. But the two who stayed are not the two the foreman would have picked.
The river floats came down light twice this season and the tally at the top says they went out full, and both tallies are in the same hand.
They are feeding the prison off the town's grain and calling it a purchase, and the price is written down, and no coin has moved.
The prison well went bad in the spring and they have been carting water up the supply road since, at night, so the town does not count the carts.
A Company man has been at the day book for a week with the warden's leave, and not one of us has asked the warden why he gave it.
Two long sentences ended early this month and both men walked out the gate and neither has been seen in the town since.
The one customer has stopped buying. The yards had ten years of that contract and four days of notice.
The yards outbid the Company on the third stand and there is a stranger the crews will not name who is said to have found them the money.
A stranger has been let into the keep who is not of the Assize and not of the garrison, and the warden signed for it himself.

helstrom.x: A Court letter came up the market stair asking after the root gallery, on account of the Drowned Tally not balancing, and Ashul-Tei has had it a month and not opened it.
Something in the gallery has been writing letters out for two hundred years and one of them arrived here.
There's a cutter in the room over the eastern sap-house looking for someone to carry a small thing a long way to a blind man in Archon, and not open it.
The rootkeeper at the undertemple wants something off the shelf above the plaza. The stair to it fell in before her grandmother was born.
People go into the hollow under the east root and come back out again, and not one of them comes back with a number. Would you go in and count?
The deep-kin hold a conclave out past the last of the tracks. It admits no foreigner, and no one whose name is not spoken by a person already inside.

The Ledger has sent a ninth man up to the weir to buy a chart off the Agacephs. He'll be fed well and he'll come back with nothing, same as the other eight. Would you take money to walk a man somewhere and not tell him where it was?

There's a Sarpa down in the deep market and he only came because a warder put a mark on the roof. Ask him about the stone country while he's here. He goes back up on the second day and he won't be asked again for a year.
Do not walk the quiet street after dark. The town will tell you that and the town will not tell you why, and the ones who do know say it differently each time. Which version did you get?
The arrangement between the Legion and the root halls got renewed this season without a word said in public, and both sides are behaving as though it were a defeat.
There is a fence in this town who has never once asked where a thing came from. Half the province thinks that is a service. And the other half thinks it is a trap.
Naheesh-Tul has stopped giving the halls to strangers and will not say who told him to. He was never told. The town cannot get past that part.
The third root has been closed since the spring and the keepers have put a person on it. They have not done that in living memory.
The carriers have raised their rate on the Thorn run and it is not the distance, it is that two of them will not walk it alone any more.
There are cages behind the Dres yard that have held nothing for twenty years, and this spring a hand was sent to clean them.
They will let you stand on the listening floor if you ask properly and they will not tell you what you are meant to hear. Half of this town has never been. Have you?
The Court sits four days and speaks on three, and the warmbloods in this town all believe the fourth day is where the real business is done.
Half the coin in this market is mudcrab money and the factor house has begun refusing it, quietly, to some people and not others.
The Agaceph guides have not taken a warmblood into the weir this season and they are giving a different reason to each one who asks.
The lodging price doubled the week the surveyors arrived and has not come down, and the surveyors left in the autumn.
The boat tax is being collected twice at this bank, once at the water and once at the office, and each collector says the other is the irregular one.
The ferrymen have started calling themselves a guild and have a book and a seal, and no charter, and so far no one has asked them for one.
A naga band came to the ford in the spring and traded properly and left, and the town has been telling it as a raid ever since. Which of those two stories reached you first?
The root halls have been carrying water up from the deep channels since the coast business, by hand, at night, and not one keeper has said the word drought.
There is a keeper here who has stopped taking supplicants and has not stopped tending, and the halls are treating that as an illness.
A copy of something went from the factor house to the Court this month in a fish crate, and the man who packed it has been paid enough to leave.
The Dres have called their factors in from three towns for a week and given no reason, and the yards here have taken it as a sign to buy.
The listening floor has been busy at odd hours and the keepers have stopped explaining the hours, and the town has begun keeping its own note of them.
Whatever the halls were waiting on has arrived or has not, and either way the third root was opened last week and closed again the same day.
The Court has gone quiet and the halls will not say whether that is grief or arithmetic, and the town has decided it can be both.
They are already arguing about who opened it. Give it a year and this town will have four versions and a song.
The fence took something off a stranger this season that he would not normally touch, and he has been careful about who he mentions it to.
Naheesh-Tul gave the halls to an outlander. He has not explained it and the town has stopped waiting for him to.
A Dres factor did the sums out loud in front of a stranger and the House has not sent anyone about it yet. Not sending anyone is not the same as forgiving it.
The factor house has stopped taking mudcrab money from anyone at all now, and is saying it never did, and half the market was paid in it last winter.

lilmoth.x: Weeja-Sen has eleven names short on the hiring list every morning and they are the same eleven, and every one of them has a family sitting in the Drowned Tally waiting to be read.
The Company hires off the same wharf at a better rate and a worse contract and the wharf has started counting.
The harbourmistress has a Leyawiin trading licence in her customs house that she has not filed. It is endorsed for the acquisition of botanical specimens and the specimen it names is a tree.
The book that would prove the gem-running is behind a warded door in the customs loft, and Tesh talks about the ward the way you would talk about weather.
Customs chained a hull shut in Oleen's own yard with her tools still in the hold, and she is not asking the customs house for them.
The key to the yard store went into the mud between the slip and the gate three years ago, and the store hasn't been opened since. Are you any good in mud?
What the harbourmistress wants is in a room with four men in it, and she keeps describing the problem as a room.

The Sap-Speaker has been down four times and brought back nothing four times, and her mouth has gone gold and her arms have gone to bark. She goes down again on the eighth day. Not one of her own people will stop her, and she has asked none of them to.

Third span on the roof walks went last month with a man on it and he lived, and the yard that owns the plank says it was never their plank. Two families have stopped speaking over it. Whose plank do you think it was?
Wide-Eye Teel has the lamp list in her head and she raised four streets this quarter without a word to the Office. Has anyone worked out yet whether she is allowed to?
Warehouse row took in nine families this winter and the row is not a place families come out of. And the Office counts them as housed.
They say the sunken well ran clear for three days in the spring and then went back to what it was. The ones who drank it will not say what it tasted of.
The swimmers have put their price up again and the harbour has decided that is greed. It is not greed. Two of them did not come up last season. Would you go down for the old rate?
There is half an hour after the fish market closes when the boxes go out and no one minds who is standing there, and there are people in this city who eat only in that half hour.
The made ground under the low city is settling again. You can see it in the doors — half the quarter has a door that will not shut in the wet.
The yard brothers are cutting on the third stand and the rootkeepers have said nothing about it. The yards find the silence worse than a refusal.
Hides-His-Foot has not been seen on the tide steps in a month and his boat is still tied. His sister says he is visiting. His sister has said that before.
Someone has been signing the Office annexe book after the clerks go home, and the hand is good enough that they only noticed by the ink.
The hatchery has gone quiet a season early and the keepers are saying it is the weather. It has never been the weather before.

Two children got into the drowned quarter on a dare and came back up talking about a lamp burning down there. Their mothers have beaten it out of them and the story is still going round. Who lights a lamp under water?
There is a man taking a toll on the tide steps who has no paper for it and the whole quarter pays him, and the legion knows, and the legion would rather he did it than they.
The organ market has a buyer this month who pays in Imperial silver and asks nothing, and the price of everything has gone strange because of it. Have you seen what a fresh one fetches now?
The ledgerman of Lilmoth turned down work twice this month. Twice. He has never turned down work in his life and the wharf has decided he is dying.
Since the business up the coast the wells here have been drawing slow, and the Office has put a man on each of them with a book. Writing it down has not helped the water.
The cutting yard has stopped taking new hands. That has not happened in this city in eleven years and the reason given is a shortage of rope.
There is a copy of the Drowned Tally in this city that the Court does not know about, and the man who has it is trying very hard to be uninteresting.
The Court has sent someone up from the rootlands and they are not staying at an inn. Four households have been asked to put a stranger up and three of them said no.
The eleven live roots are being counted again and by a different hand this time, and the keepers are letting it happen. That is the news, not the count.
Whatever was holding the wharf trade together came apart this month. The barges are still running. Ask any of the crews who is paying for them and watch the face.
The wells came back, or they did not, depending which street you ask on, and the arguing about it has already outlasted the drought.
They are saying the Count was opened by an outlander and the yards are saying it was opened by no one at all and it simply gave. Both halves of the city are sure.
A stranger went through the empty boxes at the mortuary and counted them honestly. No clerk had. Now three offices are pretending they asked for it.
The yards held the third stand. A stranger did the talking and the crews have decided that makes the stranger theirs. You may find that is a debt.
The Ledger signed terms with the yards and the whole wharf knows who carried the paper between them. Half of it is grateful.
The Court's man went home and left a list with the harbour office, and the harbour office has been reading names off it to people who ask nicely.

tidewrack.x: Everything that comes off a barge here is written down twice, and the second copy goes to Soulrest to be read against the Drowned Tally. And it hasn't been read against anything since Second Seed.
The seized hull has been sitting in the shallows for two seasons and the office keeps re-sealing it, and the seal keeps being broken from the inside.
There are two clerks here and one village and four registers, and one of the registers is for a customs house that was never built.
The drowned wreck comes up at the lowest tides of the year and people go out to it, and the office writes down who went and does nothing with the list.
Boats put in here that have no business putting in here, at night, and pay the tie-up in coin, and the clerk takes it. So who is going to write that down?
A hull came in this month with a manifest for Soulrest and unloaded here, and the office has entered it as weather.
The office has been told to expect a survey. Here. There has not been a survey through this place in forty years.

race_gated.x: The king's fishermen found a net in the reeds with a House mark on the float and they buried it rather than report it.
They will smile at you in the square and count you out of the town at the gate. A tally gets kept.
The customs house has not sent a return to Cyrodiil in three quarters and the cohort has not mentioned it.
There is a room under the customs house with a lock on the outside and the cohort walks past it.
The factor house is taking on a new hand and the last one is not being talked about.
Wagons go out of the quiet street at the second bell and come back light, and the market has agreed not to hear them.
Two of the prison's gaolers are marsh-born and one of them has been letting letters out.
Half the men inside are in for things that are not crimes forty miles north of here.
The harbour master will not deal with the bands any more and the bands have stopped asking.
Something came up the harbour steps in the spring and the town has agreed it was a story.
The sapwell south of the town has gone quiet and the rootkeeper has stopped saying it has not.
They will take your coin at the gate and your questions at the wall, and the wall does not answer.
The tariff at Gideon is set by a man who has never seen a boat and it shows in the schedule.
They loaded a barge at Gideon at night and the manifest said reeds and reeds do not knock.
The Warden-Scribe was on the other side of that desk once and she says so about once a month, to one person.
What comes off a barge does not leave Tidewrack the same shape it arrived, and the Office writes the new shape down.
Egg-sibling, the Court has stopped saying the number out loud at the readings. Ask the undersexton what the number is and watch what her hands do.
They will not hire one of their own onto the Drowned Tally this year. So there is work here for a hand like yours, and it is not a compliment. Do you still want it?
The porter on the quay is one of ours and he has been down the crypt road this season, which is not done in this season. Ask him about the tally and let him decide.
The Factor will see a Dunmer. The Factor will not see a Dunmer who came down here on Court business and is pretending otherwise, so pick one before you knock.
The gallery will hear you out because of what you are. It will not agree with you because of what you are, and the keepers would rather you knew that at the top of the stair.

w1_19_gen3_note: W1-19 round 2, gen 3 added 32 rumour rows, one per quest, for the 33 keywords that `tools/quests/topic-supply-audit.mjs` reported as demanded by a quest and spoken by nobody. Round 2 fixed this for the 32 main quests; these are the rest of the tree — Q-SOUL-02, Q-BLAK-01, Q-STRM-01, Q-LILM-01, Q-SAP-01, Q-DOCK-01 and the 28 Q-MAG utility quests, every one of which could be walked up to and none of which could be opened, because a body in dialogue/topics/** makes a keyword ANSWERABLE and only a supplier makes it REACHABLE. Each row carries `adds_topics`, which `sim/quest/topic-supply.js RumourBook` puts into `sim.quest.topicsKnown`, and each is keyed to the settlement the quest's giver actually stands in, so the gossip is local. Nothing here is decoration: under S8 there are no markers and under S35 the map may carry nothing a quest put there, so a line in somebody's mouth is the only route in.
w1_17_successor_note: RI-DLG03 §C top-up. Act gates (`requires.knows` / `forbids.knows`) are read by `RumourBook.for()` in game/src/sim/quest/topic-supply.js, which filtered on race and upbringing ONLY until this round — the flag set was already being passed in from Engine._talkPlayer() and the reader never looked, so an act-gated rumour authored before this change would have been decorative. `_note` is authorial bookkeeping for a critic and is read by nothing, deliberately.
